**Ipswich Town (home) vs Everton, Premier League match at Portman Road (scheduled around mid-October 2024; pre-match context as of 18 October 2024).**[[1]](https://royalbluemersey.sbnation.com/2024/10/18/24273056/everton-at-ipswich-predicted-line-up-new-injuries-arise-garner-iroegbunam-branthwaite-mykolenko)[[2]](https://www.eadt.co.uk/sport/24662703.ipswich-town-axel-tuanzebe-injuries-update-ahead-everton-visit/)

Only pre-19 October 2024 information is used here. All post-match outcomes or later details have been ignored. ### Head-to-Head History
Historical encounters (primarily from earlier eras when both clubs were frequently in the top flight) show Everton with a slight edge overall (more wins across dozens of meetings), but Ipswich had competitive results in some past fixtures, including notable victories. Recent/pre-promotion H2H is limited due to Ipswich’s time in the Championship. Specific older examples include Everton wins like 5-2 in 1961/62 and higher-scoring draws/losses, but these are not recent.[[3]](https://www.11v11.com/teams/ipswich-town/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Everton/)[[4]](http://stats.football.co.uk/head_to_head/everton/vs/ipswich_town/index.shtml)

### Recent Form/Results (Pre-Match Context)
- **Everton**: As of 18 October 2024, they had not lost in over a month and were showing signs of recovery under Sean Dyche, with improved defensive organization. September 2024 results included a 3-2 loss at Aston Villa (14 Sep), 1-1 draw at Leicester (21 Sep), and 2-1 home win vs Crystal Palace (28 Sep). They were building momentum with a more solid run into mid-October.[[1]](https://royalbluemersey.sbnation.com/2024/10/18/24273056/everton-at-ipswich-predicted-line-up-new-injuries-arise-garner-iroegbunam-branthwaite-mykolenko)[[5]](https://www.espn.co.uk/football/team/results/_/id/368/league/ENG.1/season/2024)
- **Ipswich Town** (newly promoted): Mixed start to their return to the Premier League, with challenges adapting to the higher level. They faced typical early-season struggles against established sides but had shown promise in patches under Kieran McKenna. ### Injuries and Suspensions (as of 18 October 2024)
**Everton**:
- Out: James Garner and Tim Iroegbunam (new issues, expected to miss a few weeks); Nathan Patterson (“not quite there yet”). - Doubt/late call: Jarrad Branthwaite (only recently back in full training). - Returning/available: Vitaliy Mykolenko and Seamus Coleman back in contention. - Longer-term/not imminent: Armando Broja and Youssef Chermiti (back on grass but weeks away).[[1]](https://royalbluemersey.sbnation.com/2024/10/18/24273056/everton-at-ipswich-predicted-line-up-new-injuries-arise-garner-iroegbunam-branthwaite-mykolenko)

**Ipswich Town**:
- Out long-term: Axel Tuanzebe (serious thumb injury from a domestic accident involving broken glass; underwent surgery to repair tendons; recovery expected to take months). - Out: Jens Cajuste (knee, not yet fit but hoped to train soon); Massimo Luongo (injury from Aston Villa game, unavailable for a period). - Assessed/uncertain: Dara O’Shea (back issue from international duty). - Available: Ali Al-Hamadi (groin issue managed with injection; back training and potentially selectable).[[2]](https://www.eadt.co.uk/sport/24662703.ipswich-town-axel-tuanzebe-injuries-update-ahead-everton-visit/)

### Travel, Fatigue, Venue, and Home Advantage
- **Venue**: Portman Road (Ipswich home). Standard English Championship/Premier League pitch; no notable altitude or extreme climate factors in mid-October UK conditions. Pitch expected to be typical. - **Travel/Fatigue**: Everton traveling from the Liverpool area to Suffolk (roughly 200+ miles). Not an extreme long-haul but still a notable away trip midweek/international break timing; Ipswich benefit from no travel as hosts. - **Crowd/Home Advantage**: Strong home support expected for Ipswich at Portman Road, providing a boost for the promoted side against an Everton team that had been grinding out results on the road. Everton’s away form was a factor in their unbeaten run context.[[1]](https://royalbluemersey.sbnation.com/2024/10/18/24273056/everton-at-ipswich-predicted-line-up-new-injuries-arise-garner-iroegbunam-branthwaite-mykolenko)

### Other Notable Storylines
- Everton under Sean Dyche emphasized defensive solidity and set-piece threats, with a focus on grinding out results amid a tough start to the season. Their mini-revival (unbeaten streak) was a key talking point pre-match. - Ipswich, managed by Kieran McKenna, aimed to use home games to build confidence and points in their first Premier League campaign since promotion. Adapting to the intensity while dealing with key absences (e.g., Tuanzebe) was highlighted. - Both teams were in/near the lower half of the table, making it a six-pointer with relegation implications potentially in mind. - No major suspensions noted beyond injuries; international break recovery and squad rotation were factors for both.[[1]](https://royalbluemersey.sbnation.com/2024/10/18/24273056/everton-at-ipswich-predicted-line-up-new-injuries-arise-garner-iroegbunam-branthwaite-mykolenko)[[2]](https://www.eadt.co.uk/sport/24662703.ipswich-town-axel-tuanzebe-injuries-update-ahead-everton-visit/)

These elements (injuries to key midfielders/defenders for both, Everton’s defensive resilience vs Ipswich’s home energy and promotion momentum, plus travel) would be central to any pre-match analysis. Sources are primarily October 18, 2024 previews and updates.

factors.impact: Everton has not lost in over a month and is showing signs of recovery under Sean Dyche, with improved defensive organization and a focus on grinding out results. This positive momentum provides a significant advantage against a newly promoted side.

factors.factor: Ipswich Town's Newly Promoted Status and Early Season Struggles
factors.impact: Ipswich has had a mixed start to their Premier League return, facing challenges adapting to the higher level. This lack of top-flight experience and current struggles put them at a disadvantage against an established, albeit recovering, Premier League opponent.

Playing at Portman Road with strong home support provides a boost for Ipswich, which is crucial for a newly promoted team looking to gain points and confidence. This factor mitigates some of Everton's form advantage.

factors.factor: Injuries to Key Midfielders for Both Sides
factors.impact: Everton is without James Garner and Tim Iroegbunam (new issues), impacting their midfield depth and control. Ipswich is missing Jens Cajuste and Massimo Luongo (also midfielders), which is a significant blow for a team likely with thinner squad depth. The net impact of these concurrent midfield absences is a reduction in quality and options for both teams, potentially disrupting their respective systems.
The return of Vitaliy Mykolenko and Seamus Coleman in defense provides Everton with more options and experience at the back, bolstering their defensive solidity despite other injury concerns.

analysis.reasoning: Everton enters this match with a notable advantage based on their strong recent form, being unbeaten for over a month, and showing improved defensive organization under Sean Dyche. Their Premier League experience provides a significant edge against a newly promoted Ipswich side that has faced typical adaptation challenges. While Ipswich benefits from playing at home with strong crowd support, which is a crucial factor for a promoted team, it's unlikely to fully offset Everton's current momentum and established top-flight presence. Both teams are dealing with significant injury concerns, particularly in midfield; Everton is missing key figures Garner and Iroegbunam, while Ipswich is without Cajuste and Luongo. For a promoted team, such absences can be particularly impactful due to potentially shallower squad depth. However, Everton also sees key defensive players Mykolenko and Coleman return. The historical head-to-head is too old to be relevant. Ultimately, Everton's superior recent form and Premier League stability, despite their own injury woes, make them the favored side, albeit with Ipswich's home advantage and the mutual injury crisis preventing a larger adjustment.
